To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
donors of blood, money, as well as time are different in sociodemographic, health-related and psychographic characteristics and that donors of all donation forms are different from non-donors.

(a) donors are a highly heterogeneous group, (b) the most important predictors for being a single or multiple donor are the number of children, the number of voluntary activities, and the number of blood donations, (c) the most important predictor for being a blood donor is being married, (d) the most important factor to be a money donor is being married and having a high income, and (e) the most important factors to be a volunteer are being married and having children.
(a) donors for single donation forms differ significantly from donors across donation forms and (b) non-donors differ significantly from all donors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of donor profiles for blood, money and time donations and the comparison to non-donations.
the identification of donor segments based on the simultaneous consideration of blood, money, time donors and non-donators.
profiling donors of blood, money, time, and non-donating individuals and contributes to a better understanding of the characteristics of donor and non-donor segments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the donor profiles of blood, money, as well as time donation differ in several aspects.
blood, money, time donors are different from each other, but also different from non-donors.
blood donors are more likely to donate money and time, whereas money donors are more likely not to donate time or blood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the donor profiles are quite similar in terms of sociodemographic and health-related characteristics, but they differ in their psychographic and geographical characteristics.
the more a person has donated in the past, the more likely he or she is to donate in the future.
the donor profiles are quite similar for blood, money and time donors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
donors of blood, money, as well as time are similar in terms of their sociodemographic and health characteristics but differ in their psychological traits.
blood, money, as well as time donors are heterogeneous groups that differ substantially across sociodemographic, health-related and psychographic variables.
the donor profiles of the different donation forms are not identical, and that the differences between the profiles of the single donation forms are not as large as the similarities.
